## Outline

- **(10m) Anatomy of a conversation.** System, user and assistant roles. The
  conversation is stateless — every turn resends everything. Why that matters
  to a scientist: context is a resource you spend deliberately.
- **(15m) Exercise: `02_plan-with-chat`.** Describe the dataset — sampling
  design, seven days, detector false-positive rate, available covariates — and
  ask for *candidate models, not code*. Push back on the first answer.
- **(10m) Exercise: `03_stress-test`.** Ask for an ecological interpretation of
  a real figure, then of a plausible-looking figure built from noise. In pairs,
  try to get a confident wrong answer out of the model.
- **(10m) Turning a conversation into an artifact.** `/plan` in Posit
  Assistant. It explores read-only, asks clarifying questions, and writes a
  timestamped markdown plan under `.posit/assistant/plans/`. Then edit it by
  hand — objective, data contract, method, **acceptance checks**. The checks are
  the part a model cannot write for you. This file is the hand-off to the tier 3
  demonstration; say so, so the room follows the thread.

## Takeaway

A chat interface is at its best when you use it to think, and at its worst when
you use it to avoid thinking.
